name: Thyroid peroxidase antibodies
rangeNote: No default range: TPO antibody assays use different calibrations and cut-offs, so a lab's positive or negative limit applies only to its own assay and results from two labs cannot be compared directly. Only the lab's printed range is used. High-dose biotin supplements can distort some thyroid immunoassays.
summary: Thyroid peroxidase antibodies are immune proteins directed at an enzyme in the thyroid. Their presence shows that the immune system has been targeting the thyroid, a common cause of an underactive thyroid.

high.meaning: Positive TPO antibodies are linked to autoimmune thyroid disease such as Hashimoto's thyroiditis. In a large US survey, about 11 % of people without known thyroid disease were positive, with more positives in women and at older ages, and many positive people have normal thyroid hormone levels.
commonCauses: Autoimmune thyroid disease (Hashimoto's thyroiditis, Graves' disease)
Other autoimmune conditions such as type 1 diabetes
Older age and female sex (more often positive)
Occasionally positive in people with no thyroid disease

low.meaning: A negative or low result means no antibodies were detected by that assay. This is the usual and expected result.
commonCauses: Rarely, thyroid disease without TPO antibodies

sources.title: Serum TSH, T(4), and thyroid antibodies in the United States population (1988 to 1994): National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III)
